lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It gives you the name of everybody who's speaking, to disentangle the multiple, multiple tracks. So YouTube—I tried that, I uploaded mine—but it doesn't sort out who's talking, so there's just a whole bunch of—it's all garbled.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: It's a hard problem. But Zoom has the multitracks. That's cool.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, Zoom, I think it's because when Zoom records, it records each—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Individual, right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —speaker as a separate track, and so I can do each one separately. Anyway, we'll see how that works. We can have transcripts from now on.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, so you had approached the ruins on the outskirts of this Dunmari fort. You discovered—I'm trying to remember exactly what you discovered.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There were two large mounds.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: One of them had skeletons in it.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's one of them; it had skeletons coming—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Out of the mound.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —which you destroyed. There were some ruins, including foundations of outbuildings. On the left as you approached, the main road led along a causeway over a dike and into a walled fort.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Most structures were no longer standing, although the walls of a central building remained ahead of you. The two towers in front were also standing, and to the right was a pentagonal building with a metal roof that seemed intact.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: As you approached the causeway, Kenzo sensed undead danger. They leapt from one mound and attacked. After dispatching them, you realized—I think Wellby maybe realized—that they were hobgoblin skeletons. And that's where we were.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And we were speculating about mass graves and the history of the fort being used to protect the region against hobgoblins. The remaining question was also that other mound, and whether it—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: —did have hobgoblins.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And I had considered using Stone Sense to see if I could.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Can I send you a message, by the way?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Also, two of you—I forget. I think Kenzo and Delwath—still have the fading bits of runic inspiration, if in the next, you know, five minutes or so you want to use that for any sort of ability check.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh yeah, I was testing that out, not totally understanding what it did.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It lasts for 10 minutes, so it lasts past the combat.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I think you also had seen signs that the mound where the skeletons came from had been disturbed somewhat recently—although "recently" meant between two days and a month. You weren't exactly sure.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: When somebody—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: That day, we tracked somebody. There was one person.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There were signs of a camp where you left the horse.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Right, right.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: And then we saw, like, footprints or something down here, crisscrossing, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes, you did. Going into the foundations.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: But not more than one person, I don't think, right?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: One person.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: So, shall we go in?

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: We go onwards cautiously, and keep an eye over these.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Before we move—this other mound here. There's something about it. There's something sacred about this place, in a way. Holy ground. It feels like somebody's blessed this at some point.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: What kind of a blessing?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: That I cannot say. That I cannot say.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: The undisturbed one?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Yeah, undisturbed.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: The green one is there. Are there ley lines and stuff around? What's the magical groundwork?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So, it takes 10 minutes to cast Detect Magic, if you want to do that.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I feel like last session we tried to do that. I don't remember what the result was, though.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, that—so that was back by the canyon.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Ah, right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Right. You had looked for whether there was anything disturbed and hadn't seen anything. Just from your general sort of perceptiveness of the flow of magic around, you don't get the sense of anything particularly unusual, but you'd have to take the time to cast Detect Magic in order to know more than that.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Can I try to walk up a little ways onto the grassy mound?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There's grass. It's a mound. You go up a little; it feels solid under your feet. There's nothing strange about it, as far as you can tell.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And I could, like, more or less instantaneously excavate a deep hole in it, if I were foolish.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's something you have the ability to do.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: We should head in, because whatever—yeah, whatever is here is still here.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: May have to—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: —investigate further after we've dealt with it.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Wait, is it still here? Did it come from here?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Is what still here?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: The footprints—are they going in or out, or both?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: They went in. Ah, make a Survival check.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Can I use my inspiration? What do I do?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What is inspiration's duration? It's the d6. Just roll the d6 and add it to the Survival check.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Nice, nice.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So, as you spend some time looking around, you feel the rune that Seeker sort of threw at you during the battle pulling you towards the causeway a little bit. Walking around, you notice the tracks definitely lead in. There are tracks crisscrossing back and forth between the mound that seems to be excavated and the foundations that are down to the left. Then there seem to be possible signs of a skirmish toward the entryway to the wall. The tracks go in, but definitely don't come out.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: So hold on. There's a foundation—like an open foundation—the mound, and then a wall, right? Yeah. So on this map, the wall is what we came through, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, that's the wall. No, that's the—I couldn't find a map that had a causeway. But there should be a dike and causeway going over the dike, and then crumbled bits of a wall. Right, the dike would be like here and there, and this bit here would be a causeway going over the dike. The tracks go in, but nothing seems to have—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: The top of the map is in—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The top of the map is—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Okay, there's no, like, giant hyena tracks or giant lizard tracks, or—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Not that. There's not any obvious giant hyena tracks, but there are definitely signs of activity here. There are a lot more animal footprints than you would necessarily think typical for some random abandoned fort in the rocky desert. It's hard to disentangle exactly what is what, but this definitely seems like an area that's been getting better-than-average traffic.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: And we haven't looked in the foundations at all, but the tracks go there. Yes, I think we should check out the foundations first.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Oh,

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Good idea. Let's investigate.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: And it looks like—I mean, it's possible, at least, that whoever made the tracks dug up the mound, right? Or it looks like they were sort of—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Definitely possible. That would be consistent with—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I hate to suggest it, but could they have been looking for something in there, and should we dig it up further?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Well, let's, let's look at those foundations. I like that idea.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Let's start with the better idea and then we'll go to the bad idea. Next.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: So I like starting with the worst idea and then working

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Fine.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Looking around, you can see, in the shade at the bottom of one of these foundations, a neat campsite nestled out of sight: a bedroll, what looks like a pack with probably food and stuff in it, a shovel, the remains of a campfire, a small iron pot—just sort of standard things like that. The pack with the food in it has been ripped open, and a few pieces of salt pork and dried fish are scattered across the ground and partially eaten by animals. It's definitely not from the past day or two. Clearly somebody's camp.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I'll climb down and investigate a little bit more closely.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Go ahead and make an Investigation check.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I'll stay up and stay on lookout.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: That's why somebody's—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Make a Perception check, Wellby. Who's investigating?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I'll go down into the—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I rolled a 13 on Investigation.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: I'll go investigate as well. That's a five. Oh no, that was terrible.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: On the left.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Down to the left.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So, Delwath, you spend some time poking around. It's hard to tell exactly how old the camp is. It's definitely more than a few days old and clearly not months old. But this is a dry, arid environment, and it hasn't rained for a long time, so it could easily be three or four weeks old.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: In the ruins, you find old artifacts—bits of metal spoons or iron nails, some shattered pottery, and similar debris. It seems like there used to be a small village or a few shops here, clearly quite a bit older than the camp itself, which is new on top of this.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There is some more food in the pack, but there are no weapons, spellbooks, or anything like that.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Any water.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No water.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Is there any indication that the person who used, say, that bedroll or the food was human or nonhuman, like from their size or other body characteristics?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Human-sized. Probably not a halfling, probably not a dwarf—unless it was a dwarf who really liked to have a lot of room by their feet. Other than that, it's hard to tell. But human-sized.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Okay, and, like, had flesh on their body and everything, probably?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, I guess it would be a fairly atypical undead who would—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Be—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —snacking on—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: —dried fish.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: The shovel was used

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, the shovel was used.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Interesting. To dig stones?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I'm guessing they did dig up the thing. So somebody was here working, and they went back and forth between the camp and the grave.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes. I mean, the tracks are old enough that it's hard to tell for sure, but it's clear they weren't being super careful to cover their activities in this area, whoever this was.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: And kind of a long time. Does this look like the main pack? In other words, whoever was here, it looks like they left their stuff. This isn't like a—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Generic

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, it definitely looks like they left their stuff at a campsite. They took water—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Sure. Presumably they haven't—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —must have taken some water and some weapons, but not their food or their other sort of main gear.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: So they're probably dead, is, I think, the point I'm after.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's possible. Well, I mean, it's not impossible they're alive. It seems unlikely they would have been surviving for some months, at least. Oh, sorry, guys. I forgot I didn't share the music. I had some creepy music for you. Here we go.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Hey, what time of day is it?

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: This is suddenly much spookier. The ruins had been pretty cheerful and under control.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What time of day is it? I guess—you got up first thing in the morning. It took you three or four hours to get down the canyon, and it was only, like, three miles or so from the edge of the canyon. So it's probably mid-to-late morning, certainly not past noon.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: So it's nice and bright and sunny.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes, it's certainly getting hot. You're getting toward the hottest part of the day.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: And how big is this whole kind of complex? Is it sort of like what you have in your background thing? It's like, you know, on one—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's fairly big; it's a decent-sized fort. The wall itself is probably a few hundred feet. It's a rectangle that's roughly a few hundred feet at the longest angle and somewhat shorter at the shortest side. The central building that still has standing walls is maybe 40 feet or so—sorry, maybe 80 feet wide. It's not massive, but it could have held a sizable number of people. In the ruins out here, there are seven or eight kind of intact foundations, and probably a fair number more small outbuildings—shops and whatever was supporting the fort. This wasn't a minor outpost. This was a notable location.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Well, I think we might need to just head in. Quickly, before we do that, though, I want to confirm with everybody what we think we're looking for. Which is to say: what do we think we're looking for?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: The remains of whoever this guy was, and why he was here. Why was there somebody at this ruin? That's what I wanted. Well, clearly looking for—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: But it seems, also, as though whatever has been animating these beasts is somehow connected to this place—has clearly been here, or feels as though they had been here. Maybe even used this space as either a staging ground or conducted experiments here. It feels like this place is somehow connected with whatever has been unfolding across the land.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Which raises the question of whether there's a source of magical energy—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: And is the guy we're following here to stop it, or to start it?

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: The timing works out for him to be starting it, or to follow the unnatural animals, or to come here quickly after it started.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Are we confident it's only one?

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: From what we can tell, yes. This person and the other campsite were just one. That doesn't mean it's the only one here.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Is there any—I mean, there are no signs that would give us any way of telling if the two campsites were for the same person?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The other campsite was—I mean, the other campsite was clearly intended to be disguised. You know, it was only Wellby's clear sight and careful eye that even revealed any signs of it. This was completely out in the open. There was very little to see at the previous campsite. So I think it's hard to say.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Did our battle with the skeletons make a lot of noise?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, a decent amount of noise, not a huge amount. Kenzo's fairly quiet when he cracks bones with his staff, I guess.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Did I cast Thunderwave? I can't remember if we did anything like that.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Oh no, you cast Thunderwave. That's right. It made a lot of noise.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Point being, whoever's on the other side of that wall knows that something's up out here already.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And it has not come out at us.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: And that's a bright, clear sky; there's no sign of thunderstorms anywhere nearby, so—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: There's no way in except across the causeway.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I mean, you could walk around the entire wall. It would take that long. There's no reason why you can't.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Might be that—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: All you can see from here is the causeway.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I still wonder if we should dig up the mound a little bit.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: The pile of rocks that the dead—the skeletons came from?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: You want to dig it up a little bit more?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: It just bothers me that somebody was here with a shovel digging it up.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Let's ask him.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I think he's dead. Maybe we find him first.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: And we think he crossed the causeway.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yes. He went in.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Let's go and—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Come on.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: This is metagame: is anybody, like, good at sneaking around and stuff? And, like, kind of—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Oh yeah, I'm very good.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: So that'd be an approach: take the sneaky approach and have somebody try to sneak in there and see what they can find.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I could definitely scale the wall.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Instead of all of us just, you know, barreling in—four dudes, like, you know.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: All right, all right.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay, so you're gonna—I mean—

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I think—what was the—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I was gonna say, just sort of sneak across the causeway and get a sense of what's on the other side. What's the lay of the land? Can I see anyone? Is there any motion? Is there anything weird? You know, what's over there? And then come back.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay. Give me a Stealth check and a Perception check.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: They're still—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Not great.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: How the—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Inspiration. I forget—did I give that to you?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: No, it's Kenzo and Delwath.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Whoops.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: But that came at the end. It's not easy to hide on an exposed causeway designed to be visible to attackers, but you creep the best you can toward one of the towers.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The causeway leads between two towers. The gate archway has completely fallen, and the towers have lost their roofs, but the towers themselves are still largely intact. You creep along the side of one, trying to blend in with the wall and rocky ground.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Most of the fort is in ruins: a series of large rectangular or square crumbled walls, nowhere higher than four or five feet. There are openings on all four sides. It seems only the southern entryway still has an intact causeway and towers, though rubble lies everywhere. There were probably towers on all four corners, but whether there were actual openings or just defensive towers is hard to tell. The only completely intact structure is to the northeast. Looking right and a little ahead, you see a fairly large pentagonal building—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: —with a roughly intact metal roof. Between that building and the southern wall is a large cistern, about 10 feet across: a big stone structure, almost like an enormous well. Its outer stone wall remains, but from where you're hiding, you can't see inside.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: To the left are the foundations of barracks, stables, or something similar—mostly rows of stone blending into the dirt, grass, sand, and rock.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Straight ahead is a large headquarters building about 80 feet wide and half as long. The roof has collapsed, but the walls remain roughly intact. Behind it are more foundations—perhaps barracks, a granary, or a stable. You don't see anything, although you occasionally catch a faint sound of something chewing.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Cracking noises, almost like some sort of large insect—cracking on the ground and running around a little bit. It almost sounds like feeding, but it's hard to tell exactly where it's coming from.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Definitely not scorpion-like? Because that would be—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, Wellby can't really get a good sense of it. It just sounds kind of like a crackling noise.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: My giant-insect sound, sir? Well—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: You will, by the end of this day.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I'll look back to you and wave—sort of give an all-clear—and wave you to come over. Then I'll point to my ear and make a listening gesture. Once you're within 30 feet of me, I'll relay what I know.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: The interview.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: And telepathically?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You can do that.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Wait, really?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, so you hear this telepathic voice in your mind saying what Wellby just saw.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: Here's the whole situation. Here's what I see. Also, I can speak into your mind.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Okay, okay.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: All right, so we cross over.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Are we crossing over? Yeah.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Mm-hmm. So where do you want to head?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Is there a map?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: I don't have the whole ruins as a map. That was too much effort to construct. I do have a few critical pieces mapped. I'm not going to tell you what.

lines.speaker: Wellby
lines.text: I think we should head toward the intact building, the—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Building? I would like to look at the cistern first.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I would—yeah, I would scout. So wait, there was the cistern, and there were some more foundations, right?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There are more foundations. There's—

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I want to see if we can follow the tracks.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: No. Yeah, good. Let's do that first.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay. Make another Survival check, whoever wants to track. As you cross over, there seem to be signs of a small scuffle, or possibly a little bit of combat, but there are no bodies or anything here. The ground is pretty disturbed just inside the towers. On the inside, it's more packed earth, and so the tracks are much harder to see. Outside of this little area of a skirmish just inside the towers, you can't see which direction the tracks went.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: All right, I want to look at the cistern.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Okay. It's definitely the top portion, or entryway, to some sort of underground cistern where water was presumably stored. I assume looking means peering down into it?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Cautiously sticking my head over the edge. Yeah.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: So it's empty now. You can see the floor down there. It's constructed ground—it was paved and then layered with clay and made waterproof—but there's a large crack in the bottom, descending into darkness below. I guess you have darkvision, right? So—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: You—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It drops maybe 40 feet. Looking down into the cistern, you see what looks like the floor of a cave. There's some rocky dirt and—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Shit.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: You can see it's cracked, and the water poured out. You can see how the flow of water washed away some of the stone and earth, and now you're looking at some sort of underground cave below, but you can't make out any details.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: There are a number of weird things about this. If there was a cave down there below, where did they store the water? Do you think they could make it if it was already there? Is this an area where you would expect giant underground caves?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Make a—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Geological—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, make an Intelligence check with advantage. Well, I guess that's your background, right? So you would pretty much just notice, but still make an Intelligence check.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: How much?

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh wait, there, it did it. I think I did it. I'm still a little confused about the D&D Beyond thing that causes the 3D die to roll, but I have to click on this thing.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: What was your roll?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Eight.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: Um,

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It's a little strange. It's not that strange. There's a lot of disturbed geology in this area, and a lot of what you've passed through since coming from the clearly unnatural canyon has also seemed unnatural. It wouldn't be unusual for there to be a cave formed by water, some sort of cracked opening, or if the land beneath here shifted. Just the fact that there's some hole beneath the cistern doesn't strike you as super weird. lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: The—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The walls that you're inside. The door doesn't seem to be locked or anything. It's a double wooden door. It's dried out some, but it doesn't seem to have rotted away in the dry desert air.

lines.text: We should open it.

lines.text: By its light, the area inside looks as if a large earthquake struck it. It's been shaken and things are cracked, but it's clearly a temple to the Five Siblings, the Dunmari pantheon.

lines.text: Each of the five sides has an altar to one of the gods: Jeevali, the goddess of life and rebirth, home, and family; Laka, the god of knowledge, agriculture, the seasons, and time; Aagir, the god of war, fire, and death—and that is the wall with the flame burning on it; Sonkar, the goddess of beauty, truth, artisans, and justice; and Chidya, the goddess of nature, the land, animals, and weather. A few of the altars are—

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: —cracked.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The tapestries and artwork are crumbled and destroyed. But on this altar to Aagir—now, is Kenzo going in, so I can describe it, or do you want to wait?

lines.speaker: Unknown
lines.text: He's going. Okay.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: There's a small silver statue, about the size of a hand, of a spearpoint decorated with an etched flame design. Its tip is burning with fire.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: That's the light we saw?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: That's the light you saw. There's also stuff strewn around. This has clearly been shaken, but somehow the walls have not come down, and the roof is still intact.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: What's the floor look like?

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The floor, where you can see below the bits of rubble, is cracked stone. It was tiled at one point, but many of the tiles have cracked. It looks like somebody shook the building and then put it back down—the walls and roof intact, but everything inside shaken.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Were some of you looking around at the magical auras, or seeing if there are any—

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Not a bad idea. We might also rest, like—

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Inside? Like, rest here, have a snack?

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Yeah, I like—yeah.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Like resting someplace like maybe outside this whole fort.

lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Oh,

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Like, all the way back out to the side of the causeway?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: I mean, someplace that feels a little safer.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: How does this place feel?

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: That weird music stopped, so I'd say, for now.

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Does it still seem sort of holy at all? I don't know. It doesn't have, like—

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: It definitely feels calm. There's no sign that anything's been in here. You don't see any bodies, dead animals, or blood streaked on the floor. lines.speaker: Seeker
lines.text: Um,

lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: I think we should rest here.

lines.speaker: Kenzo
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Unknown

lines.text: Okay. The spearpoint you see—the small silver statue of a spearpoint with a flame on top—is definitely magical. Otherwise, no item you can observe is magical. lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: Yeah, it's pretty battered, but make either Perception or Investigation, whichever. You spend a little while looking around. lines.speaker: Delwath
lines.text: Censer. Censer.

lines.speaker: Unknown

lines.text: Some candlesticks. There's definitely a collection of usually larger and heavier items left here, except for the three silver spearpoint pendants. Most are carved, decorated, or marked in some way with signs of the gods, and probably would be appreciated.

lines.text: There was something here, and something has obviously gone horribly wrong. It feels like whatever the source of that poison is, it's maybe below us. lines.text: Sure.

lines.text: Most of the skeleton's gear has rusted and rotted away, except for this horn. lines.text: Has this body been here for, like, 200 years?

lines.text: For a while. It's been here long enough for all the flesh to rot away, or be eaten by insects in the dry desert air, and for the skeleton to yellow a little. Maybe not 200 years—maybe a generation after the Great War—but roughly that time period.

lines.text: So the horn is magical, he said.

lines.speaker: DM
lines.text: The horn is magical

lines.text: What can I find out about its magical qualities?

lines.text: The magic running through it seems to be some sort of protective or defensive magic. Not necessarily strong shielding, but almost an alarm-type—

lines.text: Well, I dare you to blow on it. I'm kidding, friend. I'm tempted, though. What shall we do?

lines.text: I think we go investigate the tunnel. Yeah, let's take the light, take the horn, and go in.
